Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

VEIL#DROP Malware Chain Uses Blogger Platform to Deliver PureLogs Stealer

The Hacker News
2026-07-01 14 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have flagged a new multi-stage malware delivery attack chain that uses social engineering and Blogger pages to deliver an information stealer called PureLogs. The activity has been codenamed VEIL#DROP by Securonix. It's suspected that the initial payloads are distributed either via spear-phishing or a drive-by compromise, which occurs when an unsuspecting user lands on

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Double-extension .pdf.js executed by Windows Script Host — VEIL#DROP initial access · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] LOLBin fallback reflective .NET loading — regsvcs/installutil/msbuild/aspnet_compiler spawned by script host (VEIL#DROP) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — VEIL#DROP Malware Chain Uses Blogger Platform to Deliver PureLogs Stealer
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Anti-forensic cleanup — script-host process kill + deletion of .pdf.js dropper (VEIL#DROP) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] PowerShell/WSH beaconing to Blogger (blogspot.com) stager — VEIL#DROP
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Double-extension .pdf.js executed by Windows Script Host — VEIL#DROP initial access AIDelivery High
Hunts the VEIL#DROP entry point: a JavaScript file masquerading as a document via a double extension (e.g. transcript.pdf.js) run through wscript.exe/cscript.exe. This is the delivery lure that kicks off the PureLogs infection chain and is not covered by generic Office-spawns-script rules. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact lure shape — a .js run by WSH carrying a fake document extension (transcript.pdf.js). Double-extension + wscript/cscript execution is rare in benign traffic, making it a high-fidelity entry-point pivot independent of any single hostname. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1036/007/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1036.007 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy line-of-business apps shipping .js installers/config scripts with descriptive names containing 'pdf'
  • Admin/logon scripts stored with compound filenames
  • Software packaging tools invoking cscript against vendor .js files
  • Backup or archive utilities that name temp scripts with document-like prefixes
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","outlook.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","winrar.exe","7zFM.exe") or isempty(InitiatingProcessFileName)
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full folder path and origin (FileOriginUrl/download source) of the .pdf.js and the exact command line; confirm the parent is Explorer/browser/mail client (user double-click). 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the wscript/cscript tree, and quarantine the .pdf.js and any child powershell.exe. 3) Hunt: on the same host/user look for powershell.exe with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass spawned within seconds, outbound blogspot.com traffic, and LOLBin execution (regsvcs/installutil/msbuild/aspnet_compiler).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".pdf.js" or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.(pdf|docx?|xlsx?|jpe?g|png|txt|rtf)\.js\b"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\wscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\cscript.exe"
| where CommandLine has ".pdf.js" or CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.(pdf|docx?|xlsx?|jpe?g|png|txt|rtf)\.js\b"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PowerShell/WSH beaconing to Blogger (blogspot.com) stager — VEIL#DROP AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts VEIL#DROP's abuse of Google's Blogger (blogspot.com) as a reputation-laundering stager: PowerShell or WSH reaching out to *.blogspot.com (specifically htlwub00klocate.blogspot.com) to pull the next-stage payload. Ties script-host processes to blogging-platform egress, a pairing that is almost never legitimate. Rationale: Uses the article's named stager domain (htlwub00klocate.blogspot.com) as the high-fidelity Sentinel/Splunk anchor, and the behavioural pairing of script-host processes → *.blogspot.com egress for Defender/Falcon/Datadog so the detection survives the campaign's per-execution URL mutation. Domain is currently single-sourced (Securonix); the process-context queries do not depend on it. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A user genuinely browsing a Blogger blog (but via a browser, not powershell/wscript — excluded by process filter)
  • Security tooling or RSS/feed readers implemented in PowerShell polling blogspot feeds
  • Marketing/automation scripts that legitimately post to a corporate Blogger
  • Threat-intel enrichment scripts resolving blogspot IOCs in a lab
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating process is powershell/wscript (not a browser) and capture its command line and the full RemoteUrl/redirect chain; note the number of forward slashes / mutated path. 2) Contain: isolate host, block the blogspot subdomain at proxy/DNS, and terminate the script-host process tree. 3) Hunt: pivot on the host for the preceding .pdf.js execution, subsequent LOLBin (regsvcs/installutil/msbuild/aspnet_compiler) launches, and PureLogs credential-store/browser-data access.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has "blogspot.com" or RemoteUrl has "htlwub00klocate"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Name has "htlwub00klocate.blogspot.com"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, QueryTypeName, RemoteIp
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\WScript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\CScript.exe) @DestinationHostname:(*blogspot.com OR *.blogspot.com)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/blogspot\.com$/i
| ContextImageFileName=/(powershell|wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where (DNS.query="*htlwub00klocate.blogspot.com" OR DNS.query="htlwub00klocate.blogspot.com") by DNS.src DNS.query DNS.answer
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where (DNS.query="*htlwub00klocate.blogspot.com" OR DNS.query="htlwub00klocate.blogspot.com") by DNS.src DNS.query DNS.answer
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Anti-forensic cleanup — script-host process kill + deletion of .pdf.js dropper (VEIL#DROP) AIInstallation High
Hunts VEIL#DROP's evidence-removal step where the PowerShell loader terminates wscript.exe and deletes the original transcript.pdf.js to minimise forensic trail. Detects deletion of a double-extension .js by a script host or PowerShell — a defense-evasion signature specific to this chain. Rationale: Combines the article's exact artifact (transcript.pdf.js, generalised to any document-masquerade .js) with the deletion action by a script host — a self-cleanup behaviour that is inherently malicious and confirms live execution rather than a dormant file. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1070/004/
ATT&CKT1070.004 T1070
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Software uninstallers removing bundled .js helper files (rarely double-extension)
  • Temp-file cleanup scripts wiping generated .js in user profiles
  • Developer tooling deleting build-artifact .js with report-like names
  • EDR/AV remediation itself deleting the quarantined dropper (check initiating process)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MsSense.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "Quarantine")
Response runbook
1) Triage: recover the deleted file path/hash from EDR timeline and confirm the deleting process is powershell/wscript acting on a document-named .js; correlate with a prior WSH execution of the same file. 2) Contain: isolate the host and preserve memory (payload runs fileless — capture before reboot). 3) Hunt: look for the wscript.exe termination event, in-memory .NET reflective loads, and blogspot.com egress on the same host to reconstruct the full chain.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileDeleted"
| where FileName endswith ".pdf.js" or FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(pdf|docx?|xlsx?|jpe?g|png|txt|rtf)\.js$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileDeleted"
| where TargetFileName endswith ".pdf.js"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

LOLBin fallback reflective .NET loading — regsvcs/installutil/msbuild/aspnet_compiler spawned by script host (VEIL#DROP) AIExploitation High
Hunts VEIL#DROP's cascading fallback execution where the loader proxies its .NET payload through Microsoft-signed binaries (regsvcs.exe, installutil.exe, msbuild.exe, aspnet_compiler.exe) when direct in-memory execution is blocked. Detects these compiler/installer LOLBins spawned by PowerShell/WSH — an abnormal parentage that is the hallmark of this chain. Rationale: Uses the article's explicitly named fallback LOLBins and the cascading-execution model. These signed .NET utilities being spawned by a script host / PowerShell (rather than a build agent or installer) is a strong, low-ambiguity indicator of the VEIL#DROP reflective-loading fallback. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1127/001/ • https://lolbas-project.github.io/
ATT&CKT1218 T1127.001 T1620
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer workstations running MSBuild from a PowerShell/cmd build script (Visual Studio devs)
  • CI/CD or packaging automation invoking msbuild/installutil via scripted steps
  • aspnet_compiler.exe run during legitimate web-app precompilation from a deploy script
  • installutil.exe used by admins to (un)install .NET Windows services from cmd
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files" and FolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)" and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\azure-pipelines","\\Jenkins","\\actions-runner","\\TeamCity"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the LOLBin command line for a project/assembly path in a user-writable/temp location and confirm the parent is an interactive script host rather than a build/deploy pipeline. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the LOLBin and its script-host parent, and capture memory (the .NET assembly loads reflectively). 3) Hunt: correlate with preceding .pdf.js execution, blogspot.com egress, and wscript.exe termination on the same host; sweep the fleet for the same rare parent→LOLBin pairing.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("regsvcs.exe","installutil.exe","msbuild.exe","aspnet_compiler.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","cmd.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("regsvcs.exe","installutil.exe","msbuild.exe","aspnet_compiler.exe")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","cmd.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: .NET LOLBin Proxy Execution Spawned by Script Host (VEIL#DROP)

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

Ousaban persistence via 'Financeiro' Run key AIInstallation High
Hunts the Ousaban/Javali banking trojan's persistence: a HKCU/HKLM ...\CurrentVersion\Run value named 'Financeiro' (Portuguese for 'finance') added so the payload starts with Windows. This value name is a fixed Ousaban artifact, not a generic Run-key hunt. Rationale: Anchors on the fixed Ousaban artifact — a Run value named 'Financeiro' — reported by FortiGuard and consistent with the family's documented registry persistence. The exact value name makes this far higher fidelity than a generic Run-key hunt. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/ousaban-banking-trojan-targets-iberian.html • https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/win.ousaban • https://www.welivesecurity.com/2021/05/05/ousaban-private-photo-collection-hidden-cabinet/
ATT&CKT1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Iberian/Brazilian ERP or accounting software (a legitimate 'financeiro' module) registering its own autostart entry
  • In-house line-of-business finance app installer using Portuguese naming and a Run key
  • SCCM/Intune deploying a finance-dashboard launcher to the Run key
  • Sysadmin scripting a scheduled finance-report tool via Run
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files" and isnotempty(InitiatingProcessSHA256)) and not (RegistryValueData has @"\Program Files")
Response runbook
1) Triage: read RegistryValueData — Ousaban points it at C:\SysMain_5874288 or another odd non-Program-Files path with an unsigned binary; a signed vendor path under Program Files is likely benign. Check InitiatingProcess (script host writing the key is a strong TP signal). 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the referenced binary, delete the Run value, and force a banking-credential reset for the user given the trojan's session-hijack capability. 3) Hunt: pivot on the referenced binary's folder for FileCreated events and outbound public connections; sweep other hosts for the same value name.
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"\CurrentVersion\Run"
| where RegistryValueName =~ "Financeiro"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RegistryKey has @"\CurrentVersion\Run"
| where RegistryValue =~ "Financeiro"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ousaban payload staging in C:\SysMain_5874288 AIInstallation High
Hunts file creation under the hardcoded Ousaban staging directory C:\SysMain_5874288, where the loader script drops the steganographic image, the embedded ZIP, and the unpacked trojan binary. The suffixed folder name masquerades as the Windows SysMain service but is a fixed campaign artifact. Rationale: C:\SysMain_5874288 is a fixed, article-named staging path with a random numeric suffix — legitimate Windows SysMain is a service, never a top-level folder with that suffix — so any file write there is high-confidence Ousaban activity (steganographic image + ZIP + unpacked binary). Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/ousaban-banking-trojan-targets-iberian.html • https://www.netskope.com/blog/ousaban-latam-banking-malware-abusing-cloud-services • https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/win.ousaban
ATT&CKT1027.003 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A third-party app coincidentally creating a C:\SysMain* root folder (extremely unlikely with the exact _5874288 suffix)
  • Security/EDR tool quarantining or copying a sample into an analysis path under C:\
  • Backup or migration tooling restoring files to an unusual C:\ root directory
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MsSense.exe","CSFalconService.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: enumerate files under C:\SysMain_5874288 — expect an image posing as a PDF icon, a ZIP, a loader script, and an unpacked EXE. Capture SHA256s and check the InitiatingProcess (script host download is a strong TP). 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill any process running from that folder, and preserve the directory before the trojan's self-delete cleanup removes the image/ZIP/script. 3) Hunt: pivot on the dropped EXE's hash across the fleet, check for the 'Financeiro' Run key on the same host, and review outbound public connections from that folder.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath startswith @"C:\SysMain_5874288"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath startswith @"C:\SysMain_5874288"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ousaban C2 egress from SysMain_5874288 binary AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts outbound public network connections initiated by any process running from the Ousaban staging directory C:\SysMain_5874288. Anchors C2 detection on the article-specific drop path rather than the daily-rotating date-derived C2 address (which is undetectable by static IOC) or the Fortinet-flagged decoy server. Rationale: The article's daily date+secret DGA and the Fortinet-flagged decoy IP 162.33.179.46 make static network IOCs low-value; anchoring on outbound public traffic from the fixed C:\SysMain_5874288 drop path is the durable, campaign-specific C2 pivot. Sentinel left empty because this tenant's Sentinel schema lacks a process-folder-anchored network table (ImNetworkSession carries no initiating-process path). Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/ousaban-banking-trojan-targets-iberian.html • https://www.netskope.com/blog/ousaban-latam-banking-malware-abusing-cloud-services
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A benign portable app legitimately installed under a C:\SysMain* path making update checks (unlikely given the random suffix)
  • Security tooling detonating a sample from that folder in place and generating its own network traffic
  • Analyst/IR activity copying and running tools from the staging path during triage
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating binary lives in C:\SysMain_5874288 and correlate to the 'Financeiro' Run key / staging-drop UCs on the same host; note the destination IP/URL for blocking. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block the observed C2 destination at the egress proxy/firewall, and reset the user's banking credentials given the trojan's remote-control and session-hijack capability. 3) Hunt: since the real C2 rotates daily via a date-derived address, hunt for the same process-folder egress across all hosts rather than the single IP, and review proxy logs for the Google-page/Pastebin config-retrieval fetches.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith @"C:\SysMain_5874288"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Conns=count(), Ports=make_set(RemotePort,10), URLs=make_set(RemoteUrl,10) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP
| order by FirstSeen desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith @"C:\SysMain_5874288"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Conns=count(), Ports=make_set(RemotePort,10), URLs=make_set(RemoteUrl,10) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP
| order by FirstSeen desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user

Critical

Critical Cursor Flaws Could Let Prompt Injection Escape Sandbox and Run Commands

The Hacker News
2026-07-01 9 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Two flaws in Cursor, an AI code editor, could let a single, ordinary-looking prompt break out of the editor's safety sandbox and run any command on a developer's computer. There is no click to fall for and no approval box to ignore. Cato AI Labs&nbsp;found the pair and named them DuneSlide. They are tracked as&nbsp;CVE-2026-50548&nbsp;and&nbsp;CVE-2026-50549, both rated 9.8 out of 10 (or 9.3

CVEsCVE-2026-50548 CVE-2026-50549
ATT&CKT1190 T1204.002 T1219 T1528

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Vulnerable Cursor install below 3.0 exposed to DuneSlide (CVE-2026-50548/50549)
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Cursor agent overwrites macOS sandbox helper (DuneSlide sandbox escape) · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Cursor-spawned terminal command targets sandbox helper, dotfiles, or symlink · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Cursor agent overwrites macOS sandbox helper (DuneSlide sandbox escape) AIExploitation High
Hunts file writes to Cursor's macOS sandbox helper binary at /Applications/Cursor.app/Contents/Resources/app/resources/helpers/cursorsandbox by a shell/interpreter/copy utility rather than the signed updater. Overwriting this helper is the terminal step of both DuneSlide flaws (CVE-2026-50548 working_directory abuse and CVE-2026-50549 symlink fallback) and disables the sandbox for every subsequent agent command. Rationale: Uses the exact macOS helper path confirmed by NVD and CyberSecurityNews; nothing legitimately overwrites cursorsandbox except the signed updater, so a shell/copy-utility write to it is unambiguous sandbox tampering. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/critical-cursor-flaws-could-let-prompt.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/cursor-ide-rce-vulnerabilities/ • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-50549
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1211
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Cursor auto-update or reinstall rewriting the app bundle (writer would be the signed 'Cursor'/installer process, not a shell)
  • Enterprise MDM/packaging tool re-deploying the Cursor .app via cp/ditto during managed rollout
  • Security/AV tool quarantining then restoring the helper file
  • Developer manually reinstalling Cursor from a .dmg (Finder/installer, not a scripted shell)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("Cursor","Cursor Helper","Cursor Helper (Renderer)","installer","ditto","package_script_service")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and its parent chain — confirm the write came from a Cursor-spawned shell (parent 'Cursor'/'cursorsandbox') and not the signed updater; capture the user, device and the bytes written to cursorsandbox. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the Cursor agent session, restore the helper from a known-good build, and rotate any cloud/SaaS tokens the editor was signed into (the escape runs as the developer). 3) Hunt: on the same host review DeviceProcessEvents for Cursor-spawned shell commands referencing system paths, ~/.zshrc, or 'ln -s', and confirm Cursor is upgraded to ≥3.0 org-wide.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "cursorsandbox"
    or FolderPath endswith "/Cursor.app/Contents/Resources/app/resources/helpers/cursorsandbox"
| where ActionType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
// legit helper changes come from the Cursor updater/installer, not a spawned shell/copy utility
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bash","zsh","sh","dash","node","tee","cp","mv","dd","cat","python3","perl","ruby","ln")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath endswith "/Cursor.app/Contents/Resources/app/resources/helpers/cursorsandbox" or TargetFileName =~ "cursorsandbox"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash","zsh","sh","dash","node","tee","cp","mv","dd","python3","perl","ruby","ln")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cursor-spawned terminal command targets sandbox helper, dotfiles, or symlink AIInstallation Medium
Hunts shell commands launched by the Cursor agent (parent Cursor/cursorsandbox) whose command line writes to the sandbox helper directory, shell startup files (~/.zshrc, ~/.zprofile, ~/.bashrc, etc.), or creates a symlink ('ln -s'). This is the operational fingerprint of a zero-click prompt-injection turning run_terminal_cmd into a sandbox-escape/persistence write per DuneSlide (CVE-2026-50548 working_directory, CVE-2026-50549 symlink fallback). Rationale: Pivots on the article's specific mechanism — Cursor's run_terminal_cmd spawning a shell that writes the sandbox helper path or shell-init files (and 'ln -s' for the CVE-2026-50549 symlink door); parent=Cursor plus sensitive-path targets keeps it article-specific rather than generic dotfile monitoring. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/critical-cursor-flaws-could-let-prompt.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/cursor-ide-rce-vulnerabilities/
ATT&CKT1546.004 T1059.004 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer explicitly asks the Cursor agent to 'add an alias to my .zshrc' or configure their shell environment
  • Cursor running a legitimate project setup script that touches ~/.zprofile (e.g. nvm/rbenv installers)
  • Agent creating in-project symlinks for a build task with 'ln -s' that never leaves the workspace
  • Toolchain installers (Homebrew, pyenv) run via the agent appending to shell rc files
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("cursorsandbox","/Contents/Resources/app/resources/helpers") or ProcessCommandLine has "ln -s"
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the full ProcessCommandLine — is the write target inside the project or a system/home path (helper dir, ~/.zshrc)? A write to cursorsandbox or an 'ln -s' pointing outside the workspace is high-confidence malicious; an in-project alias edit is likely benign. 2) Contain: if the target is the helper or an out-of-tree symlink, isolate the host, terminate the Cursor session, and check UC1 for an actual helper overwrite. 3) Hunt: identify what the agent was reading (MCP server response / web-search result) to find the injected prompt source, and review the host for post-escape commands running outside the sandbox.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("Cursor","cursorsandbox")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","zsh","sh","dash","node","python3","perl","ruby")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("cursorsandbox","/Contents/Resources/app/resources/helpers",".zshrc",".zprofile",".zshenv",".bashrc",".bash_profile",".profile")
    or ProcessCommandLine has "ln -s"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("Cursor","cursorsandbox")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("bash","zsh","sh","dash","node","python3","perl","ruby")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("cursorsandbox","/Contents/Resources/app/resources/helpers",".zshrc",".zprofile",".zshenv",".bashrc",".bash_profile",".profile")
    or TargetProcessCommandLine has "ln -s"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable Cursor install below 3.0 exposed to DuneSlide (CVE-2026-50548/50549) AIWeaponization High
Exposure hunt that surfaces every managed endpoint running Cursor below version 3.0, the fixed release (April 2). All pre-3.0 builds are affected by both DuneSlide sandbox-escape flaws, so this drives patch prioritisation for a tool the vendor says is used by half the Fortune 500. Rationale: Uses the article's fixed-version fact (patched in Cursor 3.0, released April 2; every version before 3.0 affected) and both CVE IDs to produce a deployable exposure list rather than a behavioural alert. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/critical-cursor-flaws-could-let-prompt.html • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-50549
ATT&CKT1203
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A device showing 3.0.0-nightly/insiders build where the parser truncates the pre-release suffix (verify actual build)
  • Cursor forks or renamed portable copies matching 'cursor' that are not Anysphere's editor
  • Stale TVM inventory reporting a version that was already upgraded (re-scan to confirm)
  • Non-Anysphere software literally named 'Cursor' (vendor filter mitigates but verify)
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the reported SoftwareVersion is genuinely below 3.0 and the vendor is Anysphere/Cursor, not a name collision; prioritise internet-facing developer laptops and users who enable MCP servers or web-search tools. 2) Contain: push Cursor 3.0+ via the software-deployment channel; where immediate patching isn't possible, advise disabling untrusted MCP servers and the agent's web-search tool to remove the prompt-injection entry point. 3) Hunt: cross-reference these hosts against UC1/UC2 file and process detections to check whether any pre-3.0 host already saw a sandbox-helper write.
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where SoftwareName has "cursor"
| where SoftwareVendor has_any ("anysphere","cursor")
| extend MajorVersion = toint(extract(@"^(\d+)", 1, SoftwareVersion))
| where isnotempty(MajorVersion) and MajorVersion < 3
| project DeviceName, DeviceId, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, EndOfSupportStatus
| order by DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-50548","CVE-2026-50549")
    or (SoftwareName has "cursor" and toint(extract(@"^(\d+)", 1, SoftwareVersion)) < 3)
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by DeviceName asc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/

        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

            - '\Cookies'

            - '\chrome.exe'

level: high

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2023-4863")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2023-4863")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
